newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Nordbanken has no comment on article.
newsitem.headline: Nordbanken has no comment on article.

text.p: Swedish banking group Nordbanken declined to comment on a newspaper article on Thursday saying that the government is expected to sell its 59 percent stake to investors.
"We do not have any comment," said Nordbanken spokesman Sven Gustafsson. "It is purely an ownership issue."

An article in business daily Finanstidningen said that the government is likely to sell half of its Nordbanken stake to investors this spring and the second half in 1998, contradicting an article on January 3 in rival newspaper Dagens Industri.
Dagens Industri said the government was likely to sell at least part of its stake to Investor AB, the key holding company of Sweden's powerful Wallenberg family.
Such a deal would pave the way for a merger between S-E-Banken, in which the Wallenbergs hold 15 percent, and Nordbanken, Dagens Industri said.

This kind of agreement was dimissed by Finanstidningen, which said it would be against the government's principles in previous privatisations, which have been to offer everyone to bid for state shares.
